Reference implementation (Python 3.12+):
```python
def simulate_dynamic_array_appends(n):
    capacity=1; size=0; copied=0; allocated=1
    for _ in range(n):
        if size==capacity:
            copied += size; capacity *= 2; allocated += capacity
        size += 1
    return {"n":n,"resize_copies":copied,"final_capacity":capacity,"allocated_slots_total":allocated}

result=simulate_dynamic_array_appends(1000)
assert result["resize_copies"] < 2000
# Doubling copies a geometric series: total resize-copy work is O(n),
# so append has O(1) amortized cost despite occasional O(n) resizing.
```
explanation: Geometric resizing bounds total copied elements by a geometric series, so n appends move O(n) elements total and O(1) amortized copies per append.
